requirements.text: when `n * 2^64` fits in 256 bits, the shift does not report overflow, so no valid position is refused.
when the shift reports no overflow, its result is exactly `n * 2^64`: no bit is lost.
rounding down (the pool pays), the amount returned is at most the exact amount: `amount * (sqrt_price_0 * sqrt_price_1) <= liquidity * |sqrt_price_1 - sqrt_price_0| * 2^64`.
rounding up, the amount is less than one unit above the exact amount: one unit less would not cover it.

rounding up (a deposit), the amount returned is at least the exact amount owed for the liquidity: `amount * (sqrt_price_0 * sqrt_price_1) >= liquidity * |sqrt_price_1 - sqrt_price_0| * 2^64`. The depositor always pays at least the exact amount for the liquidity received.
